title: sk blend (starting)
parentNote: There is no new sound today. On day 40 your child learnt sk on the END of a word — mask, dusk, tusk — and today the same two letters move to the FRONT: skip, skin, skid, skunk. Say that out loud to them, because it is the whole lesson: same letters, same two sounds, other end of the word. The front is genuinely harder, because the child has to hold the hiss and the k in mind while the rest of the word is still arriving, and the usual slip is losing the s so skip comes out sip. If that happens, cover the k and everything after it, get the hiss on its own, then uncover the rest.

activities.mouthCue: Hiss the s with your teeth almost shut, then hump the back of your tongue up and pop it.
activities.prompt: You already know this pair from the end of mask and dusk. Today it moves to the front.
Three hisses. This one ends with a pop at the back of your mouth.
All three have a k in them. Find the one that starts with a hiss.
Say the hiss and the pop on their own first, then push them together.
Now keep sk in one piece. Three sounds: sk, i, n.
Two l letters on the end, but only one sound.
A blend on the front and a blend on the back.
One of these has an extra sound at the front. Listen before the vowel.
Same again. Is there a pop after the hiss?
Both start with sk. Listen right to the end: an n or an m?

activities.text: The skunk did skip up the hill.
Pam did skid on a rock and did land on a bug!
Can Jim skim a flat rock on the pond?

activities.title: The skunk in the shop
activities.prompt: Read the story one line at a time. Tap any word you want to hear again.
lines: A skunk did skip in the shop at dusk.
Sam and Pam did jump up and did run off fast!
But the skunk just sat and did sniff at a bun.
Sam did pop the bun in a sack and did pass it back.
The skunk got the bun and did skip off. It did not stink!
